objective: Test whether a task-agnostic compositional feature grammar can discover useful representations for unseen Boolean/arithmetic concepts rather than merely select exact task-named features.

frozenSearchGrammar.restriction: No feature may be named after, generated from, or parameterized by a benchmark label function beyond the generic grammar above.

taskFamilies.hiddenRule: deterministic nonlinear hash-derived label intentionally outside the frozen depth-2 grammar

split.train: deterministic interleaved values x=0..255 where x mod 4 in {0,1}
split.selectionRule: Candidate representation is selected using train then validation only. Held-out labels are read only after selection is frozen.

downstreamLearner: A single Boolean feature prediction, with optional inversion learned on train only.

successCriteria.negativeControlRequirement: NEGATIVE_HASH_CONTROL must not be falsely reported as solved at >=0.90 held-out accuracy.

falsifier: Fewer than three representable tasks satisfy both held-out thresholds.
The negative control is spuriously reported as solved at >=0.90.
Search complexity or candidate count is omitted from the receipt.
promotionBoundary: A pass supports only a narrow claim that generic compositional representation search can discover useful task representations in this deterministic synthetic regime. It does not establish autonomous mathematical invention, scientific ontology discovery, or cross-domain general intelligence.
